decisions.reason: As a devoré decoration line very close to the firm’s core decorative-textile knowledge, it is easy to evaluate, refine, and supply through existing sampling and warehouse routines, so management would likely retain it unless sales were clearly weak.

This transparent burnout decorative fabric fits the established interior-textile assortment and the firm’s service-based selling model, so absorptive capacity is high and the product is more likely to be kept than removed.

Although technically close to existing know-how, this burnout decorative fabric appears more exposed to overlap with the newer multi-model burnout/devoré lines, so management would be relatively likely to rationalize it out of the range.

A velour-like upholstery fabric builds on the firm’s upholstery offer and can be supported with current customer relationships and stock capabilities, making continuation slightly more likely than withdrawal.

The flame-retardant plain inbetween fabric adds a useful functional feature to an existing category and should benefit from the firm’s related knowledge and ability to learn from customer feedback, so it is likely to stay.

The polyester lining fabric with satin sheen is related to the business but is comparatively less distinctive and easier to replace with established alternatives, so management would be somewhat more likely to discontinue it and redeploy resources.
